{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"SCOPe groups d2kq5a_, d3v6pa_, and d4cj9a_ in TAL effector family a.298.1.1 because they share homologous TAL repeat architecture, not because their classified sequences have similar lengths. d2kq5a_ represents a short repeat fragment, whereas d3v6pa_ and d4cj9a_ contain much longer repeat arrays. Repeat number and experimental construct boundaries therefore explain the large length differences.

A canonical TAL repeat contains about 34 residues and forms a two-helix unit. Tandem units assemble into an elongated superhelical DNA-binding structure. The repeat-variable diresidue, typically at positions 12–13, contributes to nucleotide recognition; changing repeat number changes array length without creating a different protein family.

The hierarchy is family a.298.1.1 within superfamily a.298.1, fold a.298, and all-alpha class a. Family membership supports common ancestry and closely related repeat structure; fold or class membership alone would provide much weaker evolutionary evidence.

These entries are consequently comparable as examples of TAL repeat structure, but they are not interchangeable full-array templates. Shared family membership does not establish identical DNA specificity, repeat correspondence, or full-length biological function. Template or representative selection should consider repeat count, repeat-variable diresidue sequence, construct coverage, and DNA-bound state; the short fragment cannot represent every property of the longer arrays.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
